howTo.title: Register a business with the city
howTo.steps: If you form a corporation, LLC, LP or LLP, register with the state first. Check zoning and pick a location, then complete the Treasurer and Tax Collector's online application, sign the DocuSign email (unsigned applications are deleted after 15 days) and pay the fee. Register within 30 days of starting business in the city; you generally must register if you have a fixed place of business, work in the city for any part of seven days in a year, or rent property for business. Fees for the April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027 year run from $55 (gross receipts up to $100,000) to $60,000, plus a $4 state fee. Your Business Account Number is on the payment confirmation; new businesses also file a Business Property Statement (Form 571-L). Renew every year by the end of February.

source.label: SF.gov, Business registration; SF Treasurer and Tax Collector

howTo.title: Put a parklet or outdoor seating in front of your business
howTo.steps: Apply for a Shared Spaces permit through Public Works. As of summer 2026 there is no 10-day public notification period, so you can build right after approval; commercial parklets no longer need public seating but must be open during permitted business hours. Follow the June 2026 design guidelines.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Aug 2026

howTo.title: Get a restaurant liquor license in a priority neighborhood
howTo.steps: California ABC offers nontransferable restaurant licenses for downtown (Union Square and Yerba Buena hospitality zone) and for Bayview, Excelsior, Portola, Ocean Avenue and the Sunset (Type 87). The 2026 priority filing window ran September 14 to 25 with a $19,840 fee; if applications exceed licenses, ABC holds a random drawing, and unsuccessful applicants are refunded less a service charge.

source.label: Office of Small Business newsletter, Sep 2026

howTo.title: Make your storefront accessible
